ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle AOB = 120^\circ$, and $OC$ bisects $\angle AOB$. If $\angle COD = 20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BOD$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle AOB=120^\circ$ and OC bisects $\angle AOB$.\\
Therefore, $\angle BOC= \frac{1}{2}\angle AOB=60^\circ$.\\
Given that $\angle COD=20^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle BOD=\angle BOC -\angle COD$ \\
$=60^\circ-20^\circ$ \\
$=\boxed{40^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle AOB = 120^\circ$, and $OC$ bisects $\angle AOB$. If $\angle COD = 20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BOD$ in degrees?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the four rays OA, OC, OD, and OB all start from point O. Looking in the direction from OA toward OB, the order of the internal rays is OA, OC, OD, OB; that is to say, both OC and OD are inside ∠AOB, and D is located between C and B. Reasoning: It is known that ∠AOB = 120°, and OC bisects ∠AOB, so ∠COB = 120° ÷ 2 = 60°. Also because in the figure OD is inside ∠COB, and ∠COD = 20°, therefore ∠BOD = ∠COB − ∠COD = 60° − 20° = 40°.
